name: Andong and Hahoe Folk Village
tagline: A river-bend village of thatched roofs and scholar houses lived in for 600 years, with mask dances, Confucian academies and salted mackerel.
highlight: Watching the Hahoe mask dance beside old thatched houses, with the river curving around the village.
shortDescription: A UNESCO-listed clan village on the Nakdong River with thatched and tiled houses, Byeongsan Confucian Academy, the mask dance, Andong soju and jjimdak chicken.
metaDescription: An Andong and Hahoe Folk Village travel guide: the UNESCO clan village, Byeongsan Seowon, mask dance, Wolyeonggyo Bridge, jjimdak chicken, Andong soju, how to get there and a one-day plan.

image.alt: Thatched-roof houses in Hahoe Folk Village

intro: Andong is a small city in the hills of North Gyeongsang, and one of the strongest keepers of Korea's Confucian traditions. It has long been a centre of scholarship and clan life, and its families still practise ancestral rites. Around the city are academies, pavilions and villages that show how the yangban aristocracy of the Joseon dynasty lived.

Hahoe Folk Village is the star. Its name means 'river-bend', and the Nakdong River wraps around the settlement in an S-shaped curve. Members of the Pungsan Ryu clan have lived here for about 600 years, and the village still has real residents, with thatched-roof houses for commoners and grand tile-roofed homes for the aristocracy. Together with Yangdong in Gyeongju, it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The famous Hahoe mask dance, a satirical folk drama of masks made from alder wood, is performed on many days.

Nearby are Byeongsan Seowon, a Confucian academy with a beautiful hillside setting, and Andong Dam and its walking paths. Andong's food is distinct too, with jjimdak (braised chicken), salted mackerel and its own strong soju. It is about two hours from Seoul by train and works as a peaceful stop between the capital and the south-east.

whyVisit.intro: Hahoe and Andong are the best place to feel traditional Korean rural life.

points.title: A living village
points.text: Residents still live in the thatched houses.

attractionsIntro: Hahoe is the main draw, with more places nearby.

attractions.name: Hahoe Folk Village

image.alt: Lanes of traditional houses and stone walls in Hahoe Folk Village

attractions.text: A clan village of about 600 years, with earthen walls, thatched houses, big tile-roofed mansions and a great pine forest along the river.

attractions.name: Hahoe Mask Dance

image.alt: Performers in wooden masks at the Hahoe Byeolsingut Tallori mask dance

attractions.text: A traditional play with wooden masks that pokes fun at aristocrats and monks, performed in the village.

attractions.name: Buyongdae Cliff
attractions.text: A cliff across the river that gives a view of the village's shape.

attractions.name: Byeongsan Seowon
attractions.text: A 16th-century Confucian academy overlooking the river, also a UNESCO site.

attractions.name: Wolyeonggyo Bridge
attractions.text: A wooden footbridge across the Nakdong River in Andong.

attractions.name: Andong Mask Museum
attractions.text: A museum of masks from Korea and the world.

foodIntro: Andong is known for hearty, salty and spicy dishes.

foods.name: Andong jjimdak
foods.text: Chicken braised in soy sauce with noodles, potatoes and chilli.

foods.name: Andong salted mackerel (ganjaebi)
foods.text: Mackerel cured in salt and grilled.

foods.name: Heotjesabap
foods.text: Rice mixed with vegetables, once a ritual dish.

accommodation.intro: Stay in Hahoe for atmosphere, or Andong for convenience.

gettingThere.intro: Andong is reached by train or bus.

options.text: About two hours by KTX-Eum or Mugunghwa train from Cheongnyangni.
A local bus from Andong takes about 50 minutes.

gettingAround.intro: Buses are infrequent, so plan around them.

bestTime.headline: April–May and September–October
bestTime.summary: Andong has hot summers and cold winters.

seasons.text: Golden leaves and the mask festival.
